title: Impact of Hazardous Waste Proximity on Asthma Prevalence in North Carolina
research_question: How does proximity to hazardous waste facilities influence spatial patterns of asthma prevalence across census tracts of North Carolina, and how do these relationships vary spatially by socioeconomic and demographic context?
research_intent: To quantify and interpret how proximity to hazardous waste facilities affects asthma prevalence while accounting for demographic and socioeconomic variability across North Carolina census tracts

objectives.title: Understand the spatial relationship between hazardous waste facility proximity and asthma prevalence in North Carolina census tracts
objectives.hypothesis: Census tracts with closer proximity to hazardous waste facilities exhibit higher asthma prevalence rates, controlling for basic demographic factors

data_requirements.description: Census tract boundary geometries for spatial analysis

data_preprocessing.rationale: Dataset directly provides census tract geometries matching the question's scale

data_requirements.description: Geospatial coordinates of hazardous waste facilities

data_preprocessing.rationale: Facility points need spatial analysis to calculate tract-level proximity metrics

what_each_contributes.NC_tract: Census tract boundaries defining spatial units

data_preprocessing.rationale: Asthma data is directly available at census tract level

steps.description: Generate centroids for census tract geometries
steps.expected_output: Geospatial file containing centroids for each tract

steps.description: Calculate distance from tract centroids to nearest hazardous waste facility
steps.expected_output: Table with GEOID and minimum distance to hazardous waste site

steps.description: Join tract hazard distances with asthma prevalence data using GEOID
steps.expected_output: Comprehensive table with spatial metrics and health outcomes

objectives.title: Quantify how socioeconomic and demographic factors modify the relationship between environmental proximity and asthma outcomes
objectives.hypothesis: The association between hazardous waste proximity and asthma prevalence varies significantly by median household income and racial composition across census tracts

data_requirements.description: Demographic and socioeconomic census tract data

data_preprocessing.rationale: ACS data directly provides required tract-level socioeconomic variables

steps.description: Select socioeconomic variables: median_household_income, percent_minority, percent_children
steps.expected_output: Subset of ACS data containing key socioeconomic predictors

steps.description: Integrate demographic variables with existing spatial and health data using GEOID
steps.expected_output: Complete spatial dataset containing all required variables

steps.description: Analyze spatially varying relationships between proximity (hazard_meters), demographics (minority_pct) and asthma (prevalence_rate)
steps.expected_output: Regression coefficients showing local parameter variations for each variable

objectives.title: Identify census tracts with statistically significant high-risk clusters of environmental exposure and health outcomes
objectives.hypothesis: Tracts with < 20% minority populations will show stronger spatial clustering of high-risk combinations

data_requirements.description: Complete integrated dataset from prior objectives

data_preprocessing.rationale: All required data already prepared in prior objective

steps.description: Calculate Gi* statistics for combined variables hazard_meters and asthma_prevalence_rate
steps.expected_output: Geospatial analysis showing Gi* scores and p-values for significant hotspots

steps.description: Compare median minority_pct between hotspot and non-hotspot tracts using Kruskal-Wallis H-test
steps.expected_output: Test results showing significant differences in minority composition across risk groups
